summary: Rozszerzalny target manifest z zarzadzana baza standardu

delivery.outcome: An adopted target can extend its governance manifest while the standard-owned base remains hash-bound, upgrades preserve target additions and validation fails closed when standard requirements are altered or removed
nonGoals: No direct migration of semcod/todo2code or any other target repository
No executable-script extendable adapter for project.sh or project.bat
No authority, approval, AQL, secret, dependency or runtime-evolution change
No version bump, changelog entry, tag or release in this ticket

architecture.decision: Represent the standard manifest as a managed base plus an extendable target JSON document; use deterministic three-way structural merge during adoption and validate that the target recursively preserves every standard-owned value
interfaceChanges: new-project.package-manifest/v1 accepts the extendable strategy for structurally merged JSON targets
dataChanges: Fresh adoption materializes .governance/manifest.base.json as a managed artifact while .governance/manifest.json remains the target-owned extension
architecture.rollback: Revert ticket-024 before publishing its dependent immutable release; existing releases and target locks remain unchanged

validation.evidence: Package validation accepts extendable JSON entries and rejects malformed or unsupported entries
Initial adoption and upgrade preserve target-only workstreams and owned paths while updating the managed base
Unchanged local extensions do not produce adoption drift and the lock excludes the extendable target document
The standard base remains hash-bound and the target manifest must recursively preserve all base requirements
Removed or altered standard values produce stable fail-closed synchronization diagnostics
A todo2code-shaped fixture can add ownership for test/python-runtime.test.ts without editing the lock or weakening approval gates
